item.title: Business Interruption Insurance for Solar Installers (AU Guide)
item.description: Most solar install businesses don’t go under because of one bad job. They go under because something stops the job queue for six weeks while the wages, the ute repayments and the software subscriptions keep coming out every fortnight. A storm takes out the shed and the stock in it, your lead installer does a knee coming off a ladder, or a container of inverters sits on a wharf. The work is still there, but you can’t do it, so nothing gets invoiced.

item.title: Should Your Solar Company Outsource Customer Service?
item.description:
Every time I search this question, the front page is the same: a call centre selling call centres. The pitch is always cost savings, 24/7 coverage and handling demand surges, and it is always written by the people who get paid when you sign. None of it is written from your chair, as the operator whose brand cops the blast when a warranty call goes sideways.

So let me try to give you the honest version. I have sat on the supplier side, the sales side and the back-office side of this trade for twenty years, and I have watched plenty of good install businesses hand off their phones for all the right reasons and quietly lose customers because of it. Outsourcing is not a mistake. Outsourcing the wrong calls to the wrong partner with no oversight is.

item.title: Director Liability for Insolvent Trading When Closing Solar Co
item.description: Most of what is written about insolvent trading is written for lawyers, by lawyers. You search for what happens to a director when the business goes under and you get a wall of section numbers, cash flow tests and safe harbour clauses explained in the abstract. None of it tells you what any of it means when the specific decision in front of you is whether to take a five thousand dollar deposit on Monday for a system you are not sure you can install.
